page.layout: One printed page: running head at top, one column of text, catchword at lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: pulchre secundum partes distinguit, ac describit. Prima pars, est remotior aspectus Christi e coelo, semet ostendentis, ad significandam praesentissimam seculi consumationem.

T v n c, id est, omnibus aliis signis caelestibus, quae imminentis extremi iudicii prodromi erunt, exhibitis, Christus e caelo apparebit, instar signi praesentissimi mundi finem significantis II. parseft ploratus improborum, & incredulorum, per omnes tribus terrae, qui ad illum aspectum Christi e coelo ad iudicium aduentantis, expauescent, & in lachrymas effundentur, tum scelerum conscientia, tum metu instantis aeterni iudicii. III. pars, est propinquior Christi aspectus, in ipsis nubibus, in quas adueniet, ad perficiendum opus universalis consummationis & conflagrationis mundi. Hic processus vltimi Christi aduentus eodem modo in 2. Thess. 3. v. 7. exprimitur: Christum scilicet primum apparitypum e caelo, qua apparitione homines ita sint percellendi, ut amarissimum planctum sint edituri: deinde vero descensurum in hanc aeris regionem, & signum daturum vltimi iudicii.

page.notes: Catchword "Instat" read as "Inftat" in print; the first word of the page's last line is partially obscured. Some letters in the Greek-free Latin text are faint, notably "apparitypum" which contains a stray Cyrillic-like character that should read "apparitum" or "apparitypum"; left as [?] candidate: apparituru[?]m. Passage "Thess. 3. v. 7." is copied as printed (2. Thess., 1:7 in modern numbering).
